title: Resolved strict quotient pullback with its specified augmentation
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a scheme morphism and $A,I,P_n=A/I^n,A_T,A_{T'}$ an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $G(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}A_T}A_{T'}$ be the module pullback along the projection-defined coefficient map [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $Q,Q'$ for the source and target strict-tower derived localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix a universal total left-derived pair $(\widetilde L,\tau)$ for levelwise $G$, computed on the objectwise K-flat flat-term class [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class, lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements].
For a K-flat flat-term complex $P$ of $A_T$-modules, put $R(P)_n=P\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, with transitions $1\otimes q_{n+1,n}$, and let $a_P:\Delta P\to R(P)$ be $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. For any objectwise K-flat flat-term strict resolution $r:H_\bullet\to R(P)$, the counit formula
$$\chi_r=\tau_{H_\bullet}\,\widetilde L(Qr)^{-1}:\widetilde L(QR(P))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q'G(H_\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism. The augmentation induced after derived pullback is the natural morphism
$$w_P=\widetilde L(Qa_P)\tau_{\Delta P}^{-1}:Q'G(\Delta P)\longrightarrow\widetilde L(QR(P)),$$
with $G(\Delta P)=\Delta G(P)$. It satisfies $Q'G(r)\chi_rw_P=Q'G(a_P)$. For another such resolution $s:H'_\bullet\to R(P)$ the canonical comparison $\chi_s\chi_r^{-1}$ identifies $\chi_rw_P$ with $\chi_sw_P$; these comparisons satisfy the three-resolution cocycle. The maps $w_P$ are natural in maps of K-flat flat-term $P$, and compatible with localization at quasi-isomorphisms between these representatives. No lift of $a_P$ to $H_\bullet$ and no K-flatness of the quotient levels $R(P)_n$ is assumed.

proof.text: The coefficient datum gives the strict complex of towers $R(P)$ with transitions $1\otimes q_{n+1,n}$. Its augmentation is a strict chain map: $d(x\otimes1)=d(x)\otimes1$, and $(1\otimes q_{n+1,n})(x\otimes1)=x\otimes1$ since the quotient maps preserve $1$. The balanced tensor relation makes $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ $A_T$-linear, and these maps commute with restrictions, hence pass to the sheaf tensor products. For a chain map $f:P\to P'$, define $R(f)_n=f\otimes1$. On sections both $R(f)a_P$ and $a_{P'}\Delta f$ send $x$ to $f(x)\otimes1$, so they agree as strict chain maps. Levelwise application of $G$ gives $G(\Delta P)=\Delta G(P)$, including identity transitions.

proof.text: Put $F=Q'G$ on the homotopy category of strict tower complexes and let $\mathcal P$ be the objectwise K-flat flat-term class. The small indexing category is $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. The diagram-replacement theorem gives a strict quasi-isomorphism from an object of $\mathcal P$ to every tower complex, and says that $F$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms between objects of $\mathcal P$. The functor is exact on homotopy categories: termwise additive $G$ preserves shifts and the finite direct sums and differential matrices defining cones, and target localization takes cone triangles to distinguished triangles. Apply the resolving-class theorem. Its counit is invertible on every object of $\mathcal P$, in particular on $H_\bullet$ and $\Delta P$. This also holds for the specified universal pair $(\widetilde L,\tau)$: universal maps between it and the pair supplied by the theorem have composites equal to identities by uniqueness, and commute with their counits; thus the corresponding counit components differ by isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Since $r$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $Qr$ is invertible in the source localization, and $\widetilde L(Qr)$ is invertible by functoriality. Together with the preceding step this proves that $\chi_r=\tau_{H_\bullet}\widetilde L(Qr)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Naturality of the specified counit at $r$ gives $Q'G(r)\tau_{H_\bullet}=\tau_{R(P)}\widetilde L(Qr)$; consequently $Q'G(r)\chi_r=\tau_{R(P)}$. Define $w_P=\widetilde L(Qa_P)\tau_{\Delta P}^{-1}$. This is exactly the image of the strict augmentation under derived pullback, with its source identified by the invertible counit at $\Delta P$, as in the definition of completed pullback. Counit naturality at $a_P$ now gives
$$Q'G(r)\chi_rw_P=\tau_{R(P)}\widetilde L(Qa_P)\tau_{\Delta P}^{-1}=Q'G(a_P)\tau_{\Delta P}\tau_{\Delta P}^{-1}=Q'G(a_P).$$
Only $\tau_{H_\bullet}$ and $\tau_{\Delta P}$ were inverted; $\tau_{R(P)}$ and $G(r)$ need not be invertible.

proof.text: For any second resolution $s$, the same formula gives an isomorphism $\chi_s$ from the same object $\widetilde L(QR(P))$. Define $c_{s,r}=\chi_s\chi_r^{-1}$. Then $c_{s,r}(\chi_rw_P)=\chi_sw_P$ by cancellation. For a third resolution $t$ one has $c_{t,s}c_{s,r}=\chi_t\chi_s^{-1}\chi_s\chi_r^{-1}=c_{t,r}$, and $c_{r,r}=1$. These are canonical comparisons determined by the fixed counit and the given resolution arrows. In particular a strict comparison $h:H_\bullet\to H'_\bullet$ with $sh=r$ satisfies $Q'G(h)\chi_r=\tau_{H'_\bullet}\widetilde L(Qh)\widetilde L(Qr)^{-1}=\chi_s$, using counit naturality and $\widetilde L(Qr)=\widetilde L(Qs)\widetilde L(Qh)$. Hence it induces exactly $c_{s,r}$, without choosing such an $h$.

proof.text:
Write $B(f)=Q'G(\Delta f)$ and $D(f)=\widetilde L(QR(f))$. The strict identity from step 1 and counit naturality give
$$D(f)w_P=\widetilde L(Qa_{P'})\widetilde L(Q\Delta f)\tau_{\Delta P}^{-1}=\widetilde L(Qa_{P'})\tau_{\Delta P'}^{-1}B(f)=w_{P'}B(f).$$
The middle equality follows by multiplying $B(f)\tau_{\Delta P}=\tau_{\Delta P'}\widetilde L(Q\Delta f)$ by the two counit inverses. This proves naturality for every chain map between the stated representatives. Identity and composition compatibility follow from those of the functors and of $R(f)_n=f\otimes1$.

proof.text: Suppose $f:P\to P'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between the K-flat flat-term representatives. Apply derived change of rings to $A_T\to(P_n)_T$: each $f\otimes1$ is a quasi-isomorphism over $(P_n)_T$. Restricting scalars to $A_T$ does not change the underlying sheaves or their cohomology. Levelwise kernels and cokernels in the tower category therefore show that $R(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of strict tower complexes; hence $D(f)$ is invertible. The diagram theorem applied to $\Delta f$ shows that $B(f)$ is also invertible. The naturality equality in step 5 can thus be rewritten as $w_PB(f)^{-1}=D(f)^{-1}w_{P'}$. It holds for each formally inverted quasi-isomorphism and hence, by composition, for every morphism in the localization at these quasi-isomorphisms. For a resolution $r$ of $R(P)$ and $s$ of $R(P')$, the corresponding map on computed objects is $\chi_sD(f)\chi_r^{-1}$ and its product with $\chi_rw_P$ is $\chi_sw_{P'}B(f)$; this checks the same compatibility in every resolved presentation. All arguments use strict diagrams and the original $a_P$, without a lift to a resolution or an assumption of K-flat quotient levels.
